title: Bernard Goldberg backs a new band and Fats Martin joins
summary: After quitting a band in Dallas, Albert returned to New Orleans where Goldberg urged him to form his own band; he hired drummer Fats Martin.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Yeah, sure. Thanks Amar, what happened at the Dallas State Fair?
In what regard? Well I mean I don't. That was the beginning of my band.

You see Bernard Goldberg, a Jewish friend of mine that liked me from the first day that he met me. In fact this guy was driving a big black Pierce Hour in those days and he would go into me just like it was my car. So when I quit Charles Band in Dallas and I went back to New Orleans, he came down there and he told me, he said, why don't you get your band? Oh I said Mr. Goldberg, I'm a little too young for that. He said, go ahead and get your band, I'll get a job for you. In fact Bernard Goldberg had already had the job at the State Fair, at the Jewish. So I said, okay. I said, find out how much the men want. So I went around different guys and they all wanted $40, $50 to leave. And the one that I wanted for my drummer was Little Bob. So Little Bob told me that he wanted $40, so he came back two days before we were going to leave and said he needed a party more for his wife. Well that let me know that he didn't want to go anywhere. So finally I saw this fellow, Fats Martin. Little Bob.

Look, we never did call him Little Rock on the back. No, no. So I got Fats Martin which was a blessing in disguise. Because this guy turned out to be to me one of the greatest drummers that I'd ever heard. He had a bad tendency though to increase time sometimes. Well sometimes it was bad if we were playing a show similar to the one we played with in Detroit, Michigan. And he had this guy, Pete Peaches of Duke, had great, great dances out of the cotton club. But Pete had gone, Pete Nugent had gone and the singer. The guy could tap without even raising his foot off the floor. But he was very, very particular about his music. And Fats had a tendency to try to follow him with what he was doing and increase or decrease. And this would burn this character up. He could burn which one up? Pete Nugent. Pete Nugent. Because he raised hell with Fats about the time. But that's the only fault that I found the foys of drumming. That's why the band was considered America's greatest swing band. Because we had a tempo of the whole.
